newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent hits new highs as U.S. storm brews.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent hits new highs as U.S. storm brews.

text.p: IPE Brent hit new highs on Thursday afternoon tracking sharply higher NYMEX futures which were boosted by the threat of a disruption to oil output in the Gulf of Mexico.
September Brent was up 43 cents at $18.74 a barrel at 1704 GMT having peaked at $18.78 a few minutes earlier.
July Gas oil ended $3.25 a tonne higher at $167 about 35 minutes earlier.
"The storm in the Gulf is what took the Merc up and we are just following that," said a broker.
Dealers said the Brent cargo market was also firmer after talk a U.S. refiner had chartered a ULCC to take Brent transatlantic.
Oil products were also firm in Europe, helping support Brent. Light ends of the barrel were up $4 a tonne bouyed by gains of nearly 2 cents a gallon on the NYMEX and strong naphtha demand in Asia.
But despite the gains some dealers were sceptical of the sudden move higher. "It seems a bit strange. I wonder if the market is just setting itself up (for a fall)," said a broker.
Iraq is poised to sell big volumes of oil next month, Germany is to sell oil from stocks and North Sea loadings are not going to be hit by oilfield maintenance.
Brent has traded between $18.96 and $17.32 for over a month and some dealers see the range holding.
Gas oil lagged the gains on Brent despite getting a boost from prompt demand for good quality diesel into France.
A buyer paid $5 a tonne over the IPE into Le Havre for prompt delivery while August was done at $4.65.
